_comment: Hand-authored cross-class chaining knowledge. States: shared capability/privileged_access/full_compromise nodes that multiple vulnerability classes converge on or diverge from. Actions: the bridge edges connecting a class's mechanically-generated `{playbook_id}_confirmed` state into this shared vocabulary, plus edges among the shared states themselves toward terminal objectives. This is what turns 35 separate linear playbooks into one attack graph -- see scripts/build_graph.py for how it's merged with the per-class generated states/actions.

states.description: An interactive or non-interactive shell has been obtained on the target host, at low privilege.

detection_signals.description: A listener/handler receives a connection and shell commands return expected output rather than an error.
examples: nc -lvnp <port> shows 'connection from ...'
`id` returns uid=1000(www-data) instead of a connection error
webshell endpoint returns command output in its HTTP response body

states.description: Root/Administrator-level control of the target host has been obtained.

detection_signals.description: A privilege-check command shows root/SYSTEM/Administrator rather than the original low-privilege identity.
examples: `id` -> uid=0(root)
`whoami` -> nt authority\system
`whoami /priv` shows SeDebugPrivilege/SeImpersonatePrivilege enabled and successfully used

states.description: A working credential, API key, or session-granting secret has been recovered.

detection_signals.description: A recovered secret matches a known credential/key format and is not yet validated against a live service.
examples: string matching AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16} (AWS access key)
string matching a bcrypt/md5 hash next to a username column
a JSON blob containing "password" or "api_key" fields with plausible values

states.description: An authenticated session with elevated (admin-adjacent or full-admin) privilege has been obtained.

detection_signals.description: An authenticated request to a privileged/admin-only endpoint returns 200 with admin-scoped data, using the obtained session.
examples: GET /admin/users returns 200 with a user list instead of 403
response includes a role/scope claim of "admin" or "superuser"

states.description: A specific privileged action can be performed without full administrative session control (e.g. via a single access-control gap).

detection_signals.description: A single privileged endpoint/action succeeds from a low-privilege session, while general admin functionality remains inaccessible.
examples: POST to a role-change endpoint returns 200 and the role visibly changes, but /admin/dashboard still 403s

states.description: Full administrative control over the application: all data and all user/admin functionality.

detection_signals.description: All observed admin-only functionality (user management, data export, configuration) is reachable and functional.
examples: admin dashboard fully loads and every linked admin action succeeds

states.description: The server-side request forgery primitive can reach the cloud instance metadata service.

detection_signals.description: The SSRF-driven request to the metadata IP returns a metadata-service-shaped body rather than a connection error.
examples: response body from 169.254.169.254 lists IAM role names (AWS)
response body from metadata.google.internal returns a service account list (GCP)

states.description: Temporary or long-lived cloud IAM credentials have been obtained from the metadata service or a leaked secret.

detection_signals.description: The metadata/credentials endpoint returns a JSON object with access key / secret key / session token fields.
examples: response body contains "AccessKeyId", "SecretAccessKey", "Token" (AWS)
response body contains "access_token" and "expires_in" (GCP)

states.description: Read access to cloud storage (buckets/objects) has been confirmed using obtained cloud credentials.

detection_signals.description: A storage list/get command succeeds and returns object listings or content using the obtained credentials.
examples: `aws s3 ls s3://<bucket> --profile stolen` returns an object listing instead of AccessDenied

states.description: Broad IAM permissions confirmed, amounting to full control of the cloud account/environment.

detection_signals.description: IAM policy simulation/enumeration shows administrator-equivalent permissions for the obtained credentials.
examples: `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` returns "allowed" for iam:*, ec2:*, etc.
pacu/ScoutSuite flags the credential set as admin-equivalent

states.description: Arbitrary local file read has been confirmed, without yet having found embedded credentials.

detection_signals.description: A known-content system file is returned verbatim in the response.
examples: response body contains the exact contents of /etc/passwd or win.ini

states.description: Full or near-full read access to the application database has been confirmed.

detection_signals.description: A dump/extraction tool successfully enumerates table names and row contents beyond the originally targeted table.
examples: sqlmap --dump lists multiple tables with row counts and sample data

states.description: Attacker-controlled content is being served from a trusted origin (a taken-over subdomain).

detection_signals.description: The subdomain resolves and serves attacker-uploaded content instead of the provider's "not claimed" page.
examples: GET https://takenover.victim.com returns the attacker's own page content

states.description: A path exists to obtain a victim's live session cookie or token.

detection_signals.description: An attacker-controlled endpoint receives a request containing a session cookie/token value from a victim's browser context.
examples: Collaborator/interactsh log shows a GET with a Cookie or token query parameter matching the app's session format

states.description: Sensitive data has been confirmed extractable at scale -- a reportable data breach objective, independent of further host/app/cloud compromise.

detection_signals.description: Extracted data volume and sensitivity (PII, financial, credentials-adjacent) is sufficient to constitute a reportable breach on its own.

states.description: Remote Code Execution (RCE) confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: An out-of-band callback fires, or a benign command's output is reflected/observable, proving arbitrary code execution.
examples: interactsh/Collaborator logs a DNS or HTTP hit correlated to the injected payload
response includes the output of a harmless command like `id` or `whoami`

states.description: OS Command Injection confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: A time-based blind payload (sleep/ping -c) delays the response by the injected duration.
examples: response time increases by ~10s when `; sleep 10` is injected, vs baseline

states.description: Insecure Deserialization confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: A gadget-chain payload triggers an out-of-band callback or observable side effect upon deserialization.
examples: interactsh logs a DNS hit when a ysoserial-generated payload is submitted as the serialized object

states.description: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: A math expression payload is evaluated by the template engine rather than reflected literally.
examples: input `${7*7}` or `{{7*7}}` renders as "49" in the response instead of the literal payload text

states.description: SQL Injection confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: Boolean-true/false or UNION-based payloads produce a consistent, controllable difference in response content/status/length.
examples: `' OR '1'='1` vs `' OR '1'='2` produce different result sets or HTTP status codes
UNION SELECT payload returns injected marker values in the response

states.description: Unrestricted File Upload confirmed exploitable.

detection_signals.description: An uploaded script file is reachable at a predictable URL and executes when requested.
examples: GET request to the uploaded file's guessed path returns the output of the embedded script rather than raw source or a 404

actions.action: Use the confirmed code execution to establish an interactive or reverse shell.

outcomes.observation: Reverse/bind shell connects successfully.
Outbound connection is blocked by egress filtering.
outcomes.note: Try a web shell, DNS-based exfiltration, or a bind shell on an already-open port instead of a reverse shell.

actions.action: Use the command injection to establish an interactive or reverse shell.

outcomes.observation: Reverse/bind shell connects successfully.
Outbound connection is blocked by egress filtering.
outcomes.note: Try a bind shell or write a web shell to a served directory instead.

actions.action: Use the deserialization gadget chain to establish an interactive or reverse shell.

outcomes.observation: Reverse/bind shell connects successfully.
Outbound connection is blocked by egress filtering.
outcomes.note: Try a gadget chain that writes a web shell to disk instead.

actions.action: Escalate the template injection to OS command execution and establish a shell.

outcomes.observation: Reverse/bind shell connects successfully.
Outbound connection is blocked by egress filtering.
outcomes.note: Try a bind shell instead of a reverse shell.

actions.action: Access the uploaded web shell to establish an interactive session.

outcomes.observation: Web shell responds and executes commands.
Uploaded file is not reachable/executable as expected.
outcomes.note: Retry with a different storage path guess or extension bypass.

actions.action: Weaponize the memory corruption primitive into a shellcode/ROP-chain execution and establish a shell.

outcomes.observation: Shell obtained via the exploit.
Mitigations (ASLR/DEP/CFI) prevent reliable exploitation.
outcomes.note: May still be usable as an information leak or denial of service if full exploitation is infeasible.

actions.action: Enumerate and exploit local privilege escalation vectors (kernel exploits, misconfigured services, SUID binaries, credential reuse).

outcomes.observation: Root/Administrator shell obtained.
No local privilege escalation vector found yet.
outcomes.note: Use the foothold for lateral movement/persistence instead, or retry with a different enumeration technique.

actions.action: Extract database contents via the confirmed injection and search for stored credentials or session tokens.

outcomes.observation: Credential hashes or plaintext credentials recovered from a users/auth table.
Data extracted but no credentials found in it.

actions.action: Search the extracted dataset for embedded credentials, API keys, or session tokens.

outcomes.observation: Credentials or keys found within the extracted data.
No credentials in the dataset, but it contains sensitive PII/business data.

actions.action: Review the disclosed data for credentials, tokens, or internal implementation details.

outcomes.observation: A credential or token was present in the disclosed data.
Only internal implementation details (paths, versions, hostnames) were disclosed.
outcomes.note: Use the internal details to inform further targeted testing of other vulnerability classes.

actions.action: Validate the discovered secret and enumerate what it grants access to.

outcomes.observation: Secret grants access to an application-level service or API.
Secret is a cloud provider credential (AWS/GCP/Azure key).

actions.action: Read sensitive local files (config files, credential stores, source code).

outcomes.observation: Config file or credential store contains usable credentials.
Files read do not directly contain credentials.

actions.action: Use the XXE to read local files.

outcomes.observation: A read file contains usable credentials.
Files read do not directly contain credentials.

actions.action: Pivot the XXE into SSRF against internal or cloud services.

outcomes.observation: The XXE-driven request reaches the cloud metadata service.
Only internal network resources (non-cloud-metadata) are reachable.
outcomes.note: Internal reconnaissance achieved; use discovered internal services to inform further testing.

actions.action: Search retrieved files for credentials, secrets, or API keys.

outcomes.observation: A credential or secret was found in a retrieved file.
No credentials in the files read so far.
outcomes.note: Try reading other known sensitive paths (SSH keys, cloud CLI config, CI/CD secrets files).

actions.action: Test found credentials against login/admin panels and other services (credential reuse).

outcomes.observation: Credentials authenticate successfully somewhere reachable.
Credentials do not work on any tested service.
outcomes.note: Try password variations, other discovered accounts, or other internal services.

actions.action: Use the authentication bypass to obtain a privileged session.

outcomes.observation: Privileged session established.
Bypass works but does not grant a durable session.

actions.action: Complete the takeover flow to obtain the victim account's session.

outcomes.observation: Full control of the victim account obtained.
Takeover succeeds but victim account has limited privilege.

actions.action: Forge a token with elevated privilege claims and use it to authenticate.

outcomes.observation: Forged token is accepted with elevated privileges.
Forged token accepted but privilege claim is not honored server-side.

actions.action: Complete the OAuth flow abuse to obtain an authenticated session as another identity.

outcomes.observation: Session obtained as the victim identity.
Flow abuse works but session scope is limited.

actions.action: Complete login having bypassed the second factor.

outcomes.observation: Fully authenticated session obtained without a valid second factor.
Second factor bypassed but a further check blocks session issuance.

actions.action: Access and exercise full administrative functionality using the privileged session.

outcomes.observation: Full administrative functionality is accessible.
Session has elevated but not full administrative scope.
outcomes.note: Look for further privilege escalation within the app (mass assignment, IDOR on admin objects).

actions.action: Exploit the write/delete IDOR against another user's or an administrative object.

outcomes.observation: Unauthorized write/delete against a privileged object succeeds.
Only unauthorized read access is possible, not write.
outcomes.note: Still reportable; check for read-only sensitive data exposure (see information_disclosure chain).

actions.action: Access administrative/privileged functionality directly.

outcomes.observation: Privileged functionality executes successfully.
Functionality is reachable but performs a no-op without real privilege.

actions.action: Self-assign an administrative role or privileged attribute via the mass assignment.

outcomes.observation: Privileged field is successfully modified.
Field accepted but not honored by downstream logic.

actions.action: Chain the logic flaw to reach an unauthorized privileged end-state (e.g. order marked fulfilled, role auto-upgraded).

outcomes.observation: An unauthorized privileged end-state is reached.
Flaw only yields financial abuse (free/discounted purchase), not privilege.
outcomes.note: Still a valid, reportable financial-impact finding on its own.

actions.action: Chain repeated unauthorized privileged actions to fully escalate (e.g. self-assign admin role, then re-authenticate).

outcomes.observation: Full privileged session obtained as a result of the chained actions.
Scope stays limited to the specific action(s) already confirmed.
outcomes.note: Still reportable as a broken access control finding even without further escalation.

actions.action: Redirect the SSRF toward the cloud instance metadata service.

outcomes.observation: Metadata service responds through the SSRF.
Metadata service requires an IMDSv2 token header the simple SSRF cannot add, or is network-segmented.
outcomes.note: Try internal service enumeration instead, or a full-request-forgery-capable SSRF variant.

actions.action: Query the metadata service's security-credentials endpoint.

outcomes.observation: Temporary IAM credentials returned.
Endpoint requires a token the current SSRF primitive cannot supply.

actions.action: Enumerate IAM permissions and accessible resources for the obtained cloud credentials.

outcomes.observation: Credentials have broad/administrative IAM permissions.
Credentials have limited but usable permissions (e.g. S3 read).

actions.action: Enumerate and read accessible cloud storage buckets/objects.

outcomes.observation: Bucket contents include further credentials or secrets.
Bucket contents are sensitive business/user data without further credentials.

actions.action: Serve attacker-controlled content from the claimed subdomain and abuse the trust relationship (cookie scope, CORS/CSP allow-list, SSO trust).

outcomes.observation: A concrete trust relationship (cookie scope, allow-listed origin) is abusable.
Takeover confirmed but no exploitable trust relationship found.
outcomes.note: Still usable for phishing/brand abuse.

actions.action: Harvest session cookies/tokens scoped to the parent domain from victims visiting the takeover page.

outcomes.observation: Parent-domain-scoped cookies are received.
Cookies are not scoped to this subdomain (Domain attribute), or are HttpOnly and not otherwise usable.

actions.action: Replay a stolen session cookie/token.

outcomes.observation: Replayed session is accepted.
Token is IP/device-bound or has expired.
outcomes.note: Try harvesting a fresher token, or one from a higher-privilege victim.

actions.action: Deliver a payload that exfiltrates session cookies/tokens to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

outcomes.observation: Cookies/tokens are received at the attacker endpoint.
Cookies are HttpOnly and cannot be read via JavaScript.
outcomes.note: Pivot to performing privileged actions directly via the XSS instead of stealing the token.

actions.action: Deliver the payload via a crafted link to exfiltrate session data or perform a privileged action as the victim.

outcomes.observation: Cookies/tokens are received at the attacker endpoint.
Cookies are HttpOnly and cannot be read via JavaScript.
outcomes.note: Pivot to performing privileged actions directly via the XSS instead of stealing the token.

actions.action: Trigger the DOM XSS via the crafted source input to exfiltrate session data.

outcomes.observation: Cookies/tokens are received at the attacker endpoint.
Cookies are HttpOnly and cannot be read via JavaScript.

actions.action: Use the smuggling primitive to capture another user's request/response.

outcomes.observation: A victim's session data is captured.
Desync confirmed but only usable for cache poisoning at scale, not direct capture.
outcomes.note: See cache poisoning chain for the mass-impact variant.

actions.action: Poison the shared cache with a payload that exfiltrates victim session data at scale.

outcomes.observation: Poisoned response harvests session data from multiple victims.
Poisoning only achieves denial of service (error responses cached).

actions.action: Chain the CSRF against a state-changing endpoint that grants privileges (e.g. add attacker as admin, change victim's email).

outcomes.observation: A privileged endpoint is reachable via CSRF.
No privileged endpoint is CSRF-able from this vector.
outcomes.note: Impact limited to the specific action already confirmed.

actions.action: Chain the open redirect with an in-scope OAuth/SSO flow to leak authorization codes/tokens to an attacker-controlled domain.

outcomes.observation: An authorization code/token is leaked via the redirect chain.
No OAuth/SSO flow is in scope to chain with.
outcomes.note: Primarily useful for phishing without a chainable flow.

actions.action: Read authenticated API responses cross-origin using the credentialed CORS misconfiguration.

outcomes.observation: Sensitive account/business data is read cross-origin.
A session token/API key is present in the read response.

actions.action: Query under-protected fields/mutations discovered via introspection.

outcomes.observation: Sensitive data is returned by an under-protected field.
An under-protected mutation performs a privileged action.

actions.action: Chain the pollution with a security-sensitive gadget (auth-check default, template-rendering flag).

outcomes.observation: A gadget consuming the polluted property grants privilege.
A gadget consuming the polluted property triggers script execution.

actions.action: Chain the clickjacking UI-redress to trick a victim into performing a privileged action.

outcomes.observation: A victim click triggers a privileged state change.
Only a non-privileged action could be framed.
